intent.raw_query: Cambodia Angkor Wat + beaches, $1100, 10 days, November 2026

experiences.name: Angkor Wat Temple Complex
experiences.description: Explore the world's largest religious monument at sunrise, wandering through the iconic towers and intricate bas-reliefs of this 12th-century Khmer masterpiece. Book a tuk-tuk from Siem Reap old market area for easy access. Given late flight arrival on Day 1, plan this for Day 2 morning after a full night's rest at a hotel within 15 minutes of the temple gates.

experiences.name: Phnom Penh Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda
experiences.description: Visit the stunning royal residence and the Silver Pagoda, home to a life-sized gold Buddha encrusted with diamonds. Located in the heart of Phnom Penh near riverside hotels, making it ideal for an afternoon arrival day activity if you adjust your flight to land by early afternoon instead of 20:00+, maximizing Day 1 sightseeing.

experiences.name: Koh Rong Samloem Beach Escape
experiences.description: Spend two days on this pristine island with turquoise waters and white sand beaches. Take a ferry from Sihanoukville port. Stay in beachfront bungalows on Saracen Bay, which is within walking distance of snorkeling spots and jungle trails. Best enjoyed mid-trip after cultural days in Phnom Penh.
experiences.location: Saracen Bay, Koh Rong Samloem Island

experiences.name: Phsar Thmei Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided street food walking tour through Phnom Penh's iconic Art Deco Central Market, sampling amok fish curry, nom banh chok noodles, and fresh tropical fruits. Staying near the riverside or BKK1 district puts you within a 10-minute tuk-tuk ride, making this a perfect half-day activity without long transfers.
experiences.location: Phsar Thmei (Central Market), Daun Penh, Phnom Penh

experiences.name: Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum and Killing Fields
experiences.description: A deeply moving and essential historical experience documenting the Khmer Rouge era at the former S-21 prison and Choeung Ek memorial. Both sites are located in or near central Phnom Penh, easily accessible from riverside hotels. Plan this for a morning on a mid-trip day to allow time for reflection in the afternoon.
experiences.location: Tuol Sleng, Phnom Penh and Choeung Ek, outskirts of Phnom Penh

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cambodia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into Siem Reap Boutique Stay. Take a leisurely walk around the Old Market (Phsar Chas) area to get oriented, pick up a local SIM card, and exchange currency at a local money changer for better rates.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Pub Street and the surrounding alleyways to soak in the lively atmosphere. Visit the Night Market for cheap souvenirs and street snacks. Watch local Apsara dance performances sometimes offered for free outside restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a snack on the plane
meals.lunch: Grab a quick $2–3 bowl of Khmer noodle soup (Kuy Teav) from a street stall near the airport or Old Market area
meals.dinner: Dinner at Khmer Kitchen Restaurant near Pub Street — hearty Khmer dishes for $3–5 per person

day_by_day.notes: November is the tail end of the rainy season in Cambodia — expect warm weather around 28–32°C with occasional short showers. Carry a light rain jacket. Tuk-tuks from the airport to the hotel cost around $8–10; negotiate beforehand.

day_by_day.morning: Early start (5:30 AM) to watch sunrise at Angkor Wat — one of the most iconic experiences in Southeast Asia. Purchase a 3-day Angkor Pass ($62) for maximum value over the next few days. Explore the outer galleries and the main temple complex.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Angkor Thom complex: visit the Bayon Temple with its famous stone faces, the Baphuon, Phimeanakas, and the Terrace of the Elephants. Hire a tuk-tuk driver for the day ($15–18) to cover the distances comfortably.
day_by_day.evening: Return to town and visit the vibrant Angkor Night Market. Browse handmade crafts and enjoy a $1 fresh fruit shake. Watch a free traditional Khmer shadow puppet show if available.

meals.breakfast: Grab a baguette sandwich ($1–2) and coffee from a street cart near the hotel before heading out
meals.lunch: Pack a simple lunch or eat at one of the basic local stalls near the Angkor complex for $2–4
meals.dinner: Try Mahob Restaurant for authentic Cambodian cuisine — budget around $5–7 per person

day_by_day.notes: Start as early as possible (5:00–5:30 AM) for sunrise at Angkor Wat to beat the crowds. Bring plenty of water and sunscreen. Dress modestly — shoulders and knees must be covered to enter temples.

day_by_day.morning: Use Day 2 of your Angkor Pass to visit the jungle temple of Ta Prohm (the 'Tomb Raider' temple), famous for massive tree roots engulfing the ancient stone structures. Arrive early to enjoy it before crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Banteay Kdei and the nearby Srah Srang reservoir — a peaceful spot for photos. Then head to Banteay Srei temple (about 25 km away), renowned for its intricate pink sandstone carvings and excellent preservation.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Siem Reap's vibrant local scene at the Made in Cambodia Market. Enjoy a traditional Khmer massage at one of the affordable spas along Sivatha Boulevard ($8–10 for one hour).

meals.breakfast: Rice porridge (Bobor) from a local market stall — $1–2
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside stall near Banteay Srei — $2–3
meals.dinner: Eat at a local Khmer BBQ restaurant (Siem Reap has many) — grill your own meats and veggies for around $5–8 per person

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei is farther out so factor in extra tuk-tuk costs — negotiate a full-day tuk-tuk for $18–22. The intricate carvings at Banteay Srei are best photographed in morning or late afternoon light.

day_by_day.morning: Use Day 3 of your Angkor Pass to visit the lesser-known but stunning Preah Khan temple — large, atmospheric, and far less crowded than Angkor Wat. Explore the long corridors and moss-covered stones at your own pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Neak Pean (a small island temple on an artificial lake) and Ta Som temple. Afterward, stop by the Angkor National Museum in town ($12 entry) to deepen your understanding of Khmer history and civilization.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost cultural show at one of the local restaurants. Try watching a live Apsara dance performance at Koulen Restaurant (dinner + show package around $12–15).

meals.breakfast: French-style breakfast at a local bakery café — $2–3
meals.lunch: Local rice and curry plate near the temple area — $2–3
meals.dinner: Dinner included in Apsara show package, or eat beforehand at a street food stall for $3–4

day_by_day.notes: This is your last day using the Angkor Pass — make the most of it. Angkor National Museum is optional but highly educational and worth the entry fee for history lovers.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Cambodian Landmine Museum (free entry, donations welcome) — a sobering and important cultural experience about Cambodia's recent history. Located about 25 km from Siem Reap near the Angkor temples.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the floating village of Kompong Phluk on Tonle Sap Lake — a unique experience of stilted wooden houses rising high above the water. Boat tours cost around $15–20 per person but can be split with other travelers.
day_by_day.evening: Back in town, wander through the local Kandal Village neighborhood — a quieter, artsy area with indie cafés, boutique shops, and local galleries. Enjoy a sunset drink at a rooftop bar.

meals.breakfast: Sticky rice with mango from a street vendor — $1
meals.lunch: Fish amok (Cambodia's national dish) at a local restaurant — $3–5
meals.dinner: Street food dinner at the Old Market area — try grilled corn, spring rolls, and noodle dishes for under $4 total

day_by_day.notes: The Landmine Museum is deeply moving and provides important context about Cambodia's history with the Khmer Rouge era. Tonle Sap Lake is one of the largest freshwater lakes in Southeast Asia — water levels are high in November, making it an ideal time to visit.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning bus or shared minivan from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh (approximately 6 hours, $6–10). Book with Giant Ibis or Mekong Express for reliable service. Enjoy the countryside scenery along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh around midday. Check into a budget guesthouse ($8–15/night). Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda (entry $10) — stunning examples of Khmer royal architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Sisowath Quay riverside promenade as the sun sets over the Mekong and Tonle Sap rivers. Browse the night market stalls and enjoy the lively local atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Quick bite before boarding the bus — bread and coffee for $1–2
meals.lunch: Eat on the road or at a rest stop — rice dishes for $2–3
meals.dinner: Dinner at a riverside restaurant along Sisowath Quay — try Khmer curry for $4–6

day_by_day.notes: Book your bus ticket a day in advance to secure a seat. Giant Ibis is slightly pricier but more reliable and comfortable. Phnom Penh budget guesthouses are plentiful around the BKK1 and Riverside areas.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a former high school turned Khmer Rouge detention center, now a powerful memorial. Entry is $5. This is a deeply emotional but essential historical site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a tuk-tuk to the Choeung Ek Killing Fields Memorial ($6 entry, audio guide included) — located about 15 km outside the city center. The audio guide is excellent and deeply informative.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city and explore the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) — a stunning Art Deco yellow dome structure. Browse local goods and pick up affordable souvenirs. Enjoy dinner in the lively street food scene nearby.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi (Cambodian baguette sandwich) from a street stall — $1
meals.lunch: Simple rice and vegetable dish near Tuol Sleng — $2–3
meals.dinner: Street food near Central Market — lok lak (stir-fried beef with rice) for $3–4

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Killing Fields visits are emotionally heavy — allow yourself time to process. Consider visiting in the morning when you're more mentally fresh. These sites are essential for understanding modern Cambodian history.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early bus or shared taxi from Phnom Penh to Sihanoukville (approximately 4 hours, $6–9). Alternatively, book a direct bus to Otres Beach area for a quieter, more budget-friendly beach experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Sihanoukville / Otres Beach. Check into a budget beach bungalow or guesthouse ($10–20/night). Spend the afternoon relaxing on the beach, swimming in the warm Gulf of Thailand waters.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset beach walk and watch the fishing boats return. Grab dinner at one of the casual beachside shacks — fresh seafood is affordable and delicious here.

meals.breakfast: Eat before boarding the bus — $1–2 street food
meals.lunch: Grab food at a bus stop or arrive and eat at a beachside café — $3–4
meals.dinner: Fresh grilled seafood platter at a beachside shack — prawns, fish, and squid for $5–8

day_by_day.notes: Otres Beach is recommended over the main Serendipity Beach area in Sihanoukville, which has become heavily commercialized. Otres retains a quieter, more backpacker-friendly vibe with budget accommodation options. November weather should be warm and mostly dry on the coast.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle or motorbike ($5–8/day) and explore the Sihanoukville peninsula. Visit Sokha Beach and Independence Beach for a change of scenery. Stop at a local fishing village to see traditional boat-building and fishing culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a boat trip to one of the nearby islands — Koh Rong Samloem is the most popular for budget travelers (boat ticket $20–25 return). Spend a few hours snorkeling in crystal-clear waters, exploring coral reefs, and relaxing on pristine white sand.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Otres Beach by late afternoon. Enjoy a relaxing evening with a beach bonfire (if available at your guesthouse) or join other travelers for a casual dinner and drinks at a beachside bar.

meals.breakfast: Fruit smoothie bowl and toast at a beach café — $2–3
meals.lunch: Pack a simple lunch or eat on the island — fresh coconut and snacks $2–4
meals.dinner: BBQ dinner at a beachside restaurant — $5–7 for grilled fish with rice and vegetables

day_by_day.notes: Book the island boat trip the evening before to confirm schedules. Koh Rong Samloem's Lazy Beach and Saracen Bay are stunning. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, snorkeling gear (can rent for $3–5), and plenty of water. Check sea conditions as November can occasionally bring choppy waters.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final leisurely morning on Otres Beach — swim, read, or take a sunrise walk along the shoreline. Pack up and check out of accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a bus or shared taxi back to Phnom Penh (4 hours) or directly to Siem Reap (7–8 hours) depending on your departure flight. If time allows before departure, stop at a local market to pick up last-minute souvenirs like Kampot pepper, silk scarves, or handmade crafts.
day_by_day.evening: If departing from Phnom Penh, enjoy a final Cambodian meal near the airport or city center before heading to the airport. Reflect on an incredible 10-day journey through Cambodia's history, culture, and beaches.

meals.breakfast: Final beach breakfast — Khmer-style omelette with baguette and iced coffee — $2–3
meals.lunch: Quick lunch at a roadside stop or bus terminal — $2–3
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a local restaurant — amok fish curry or Khmer beef lok lak — $4–6

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your return transport booking the night before. Budget approximately $6–10 for the bus back. If flying out of Phnom Penh, allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Total estimated 10-day budget (excluding flights): $250–350 USD covering accommodation, transport, food, and key attractions.

trip_options.title: Classic Cambodia Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Siem Reap Boutique Stay, check in, freshen up, and rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk around the hotel neighborhood. Stroll through the Old Market (Psar Chas) area to get acquainted with local sights, sounds, and smells. Browse handicrafts and pick up any essentials.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Pub Street and the surrounding alleyways for a lively introduction to Siem Reap's nightlife and street food scene. Watch a free traditional Apsara dance performance if available at a nearby restaurant.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: Grab a light meal or snack at the airport or upon arrival at a local café near the hotel (~$5–8)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mahob Restaurant on Pub Street — authentic Khmer cuisine in a mid-range setting (~$10–15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light due to travel fatigue. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance. Exchange currency or withdraw Cambodian Riel/USD at the airport ATM.

day_by_day.morning: Early visit to Angkor Wat at sunrise (depart hotel by 5:00 AM). Watch the iconic sunrise reflection over the main temple, then explore the outer galleries, bas-reliefs depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk, and the central towers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Angkor Thom complex — visit the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces, the Baphuon, Elephant Terrace, and the Terrace of the Leper King. Enjoy a packed lunch or eat at one of the on-site food stalls.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap. Relax at the hotel, then head to Kandal Village for dinner in a quieter, boutique-café neighborhood away from the tourist crowds.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel or grab a baguette and coffee from a street vendor before sunrise (~$3–5)
meals.lunch: Local noodle soup or rice dish at an Angkor complex food stall (~$4–6)
meals.dinner: Cuisine Wat Damnak — award-winning modern Khmer tasting menu (mid-range splurge, ~$20–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a 3-day Angkor Pass ($62 USD) — it offers the best value and covers multiple days. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water. November weather is generally dry and pleasant.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ta Prohm temple — the famous 'jungle temple' where massive tree roots engulf ancient stone walls, famously used in the Tomb Raider film. Arrive early to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Banteay Kdei and the nearby Srah Srang reservoir (a beautiful royal bathing pool). Then visit Pre Rup temple for panoramic views over the surrounding jungle.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Angkor National Museum in Siem Reap for deeper historical and cultural context on the Khmer Empire (~$12 entry). Great air-conditioned way to spend the early evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at a local café such as The Blue Pumpkin (~$5–8)
meals.lunch: Brown Rice Café near the temples — vegetarian-friendly, mid-range (~$6–10)
meals.dinner: Malis Restaurant — upscale Khmer cuisine with a garden setting (~$15–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 of your Angkor Pass. Rent a tuk-tuk for the day (~$15–20) for flexibility between temple sites. Comfortable walking shoes are essential.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Banteay Srei — a stunning 10th-century temple known for its intricate pink sandstone carvings, located about 25 km north of Siem Reap. One of the finest examples of Khmer art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the Landmine Museum on the way back — a sobering and important cultural experience that tells the story of Cambodia's tragic recent history and ongoing demining efforts (~$5 donation).
day_by_day.evening: Visit Artisans Angkor workshop and showroom in Siem Reap — watch local craftspeople create silk, lacquerware, and stone carvings. Browse for authentic souvenirs that support local artisans.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel (~included or $5–8)
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch from a local market or eat at a roadside Khmer restaurant near Banteay Srei (~$5–7)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Haven Restaurant — a social enterprise training at-risk youth in culinary arts. Excellent food with a meaningful cause (~$10–15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 3 of your Angkor Pass — use it wisely at Banteay Srei. Hire a knowledgeable tuk-tuk driver who can serve as an informal guide for the day (~$20–25 for the full day trip).

day_by_day.morning: Departure from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh by express bus or domestic flight (~6 hours by bus / 45 min by flight). Scenic bus ride along the Tonle Sap lake region is recommended for budget travelers (~$10–15 by bus).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh. Check into a mid-range guesthouse or hotel near the riverside. Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — a magnificent complex of royal buildings and the famous floor made of 5,000 silver tiles (~$10 entry).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Sisowath Quay (riverfront promenade) as the sun sets over the Tonle Sap and Mekong rivers. Enjoy the lively atmosphere with street food vendors and riverside bars.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel in Siem Reap before departure (~$5–8)
meals.lunch: Snack or meal during the bus journey or upon arrival in Phnom Penh at a riverside café (~$5–8)
meals.dinner: Romdeng Restaurant — Phnom Penh's iconic restaurant serving traditional Cambodian cuisine including exotic dishes, run by a social enterprise (~$12–18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book bus or flight tickets in advance. Giant Ibis Bus is highly recommended for comfort and reliability. Phnom Penh accommodation: aim for a riverside guesthouse ($25–50/night).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a deeply moving and historically essential experience documenting the Khmer Rouge atrocities. Allow 2–3 hours (~$5 entry, audio guide recommended).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Killing Fields of Choeung Ek, located 15 km outside the city (~$6 entry with audio guide). The memorial stupa and serene grounds provide a contemplative space to reflect on Cambodia's history.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Central Market (Psar Thmei) — a stunning Art Deco building housing a maze of stalls selling jewelry, clothing, and local goods. Then enjoy a sunset cocktail at a rooftop bar overlooking the city.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel (~$5–8)
meals.lunch: Friends the Restaurant (Phnom Penh) — another social enterprise training street youth, serving tapas-style Khmer food (~$8–12)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a riverside restaurant such as Khmer Surin — traditional Khmer dishes in a relaxed setting (~$10–15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Killing Fields visits are emotionally heavy — take breaks and be respectful. Dress conservatively. Hiring a tuk-tuk for the day in Phnom Penh is recommended (~$15–20).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Cambodia — home to the world's finest collection of Khmer art and sculpture, including pre-Angkorian bronzes and stone statues (~$10 entry). Spend 1.5–2 hours here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel from Phnom Penh to Sihanoukville by bus (~4–5 hours, ~$10–12) or take a direct bus to Kampot (~4 hours, ~$8–10). Kampot is highly recommended for a more authentic, relaxed beach-adjacent experience.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Kampot. Check into a riverside guesthouse or eco-lodge. Take an easy evening stroll through the charming French colonial town center with its pastel-colored buildings and quiet riverside.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel in Phnom Penh (~$5–8)
meals.lunch: Eat before or during the bus journey — grab supplies from a local market or eat at a roadside stop (~$4–6)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Rikitikitavi Restaurant in Kampot — riverside dining with a great menu of Khmer and Western food (~$10–15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Kampot is a more peaceful and authentic alternative to Sihanoukville, which has undergone significant development. Kampot is famous for its pepper plantations and is a great base for beach and nature activities.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kep — a charming seaside town 25 km from Kampot, known for its famous Crab Market and beautiful coastal scenery. Rent a motorbike or take a tuk-tuk (~$10–15 round trip).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kep National Park — hike through jungle trails with views over the Gulf of Thailand and Rabbit Island (Koh Tonsay). Alternatively, take a short boat trip to Rabbit Island for a few hours on a pristine beach (~$5 boat fare).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kampot. Take a sunset boat cruise along the Kampot River through mangroves — a magical experience as fireflies light up the trees after dark (~$8–12 per person).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the guesthouse or a local café in Kampot (~$4–7)
meals.lunch: Fresh crab with Kampot pepper sauce at the Kep Crab Market — a must-try culinary experience (~$10–15)
meals.dinner: Rusty Keyhole or Epic Arts Café in Kampot — relaxed riverside dining with a social enterprise focus (~$8–12 per person)

day_by_day.notes: November is the beginning of Cambodia's dry season — weather in Kampot and Kep should be warm and sunny with low humidity. Ideal beach conditions. Apply reef-safe sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a Kampot Pepper Plantation — the region is world-famous for its unique pepper. Take a guided tour to learn about the cultivation process and history of this prized spice (~$5–10 tour fee). Buy some to take home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Bokor Hill Station — a mysterious abandoned French colonial resort and casino perched atop a mountain with sweeping views over the Gulf of Thailand. Accessible by motorbike or tuk-tuk (~$15–20 for transport).
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Kampot. Enjoy a relaxed sunset from a riverside bar. Visit the Old French Quarter for a last walk through the colonial architecture. Pack for the journey back.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the guesthouse (~$4–7)
meals.lunch: Picnic or snack at Bokor Hill Station, or eat at the mountaintop restaurant with panoramic views (~$6–10)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Baraka Restaurant in Kampot — organic, locally sourced ingredients with a great atmosphere (~$10–15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The road to Bokor can be misty and windy — bring a light jacket. The abandoned ghost-town atmosphere of Bokor is eerie and fascinating. Purchase Kampot pepper as a unique souvenir.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Kampot. Enjoy a slow breakfast by the river, do any last-minute souvenir shopping, and check out of the guesthouse. Take a bus or shared taxi back to Phnom Penh (~4 hours) for onward travel.
day_by_day.afternoon: If time permits before your departure flight, revisit the Phnom Penh riverfront for a final stroll or visit a local spa for a traditional Khmer massage (~$15–25/hour) as a relaxing end to the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Phnom Penh International Airport for departure. Reflect on 10 incredible days exploring Cambodia's ancient temples, poignant history, vibrant culture, and beautiful coastline.

meals.breakfast: Final Cambodian breakfast — try Bai Sach Chrouk (grilled pork and rice) from a local street stall (~$2–3)
meals.lunch: Light meal in Phnom Penh near the airport or riverfront (~$6–10)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or meal before departure (~$8–15)

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the airport at least 2–3 hours before international departure. Keep some USD cash for airport taxes or last-minute purchases. Cambodian Riel cannot be easily exchanged outside Cambodia — spend remaining Riel before departure.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Cambodia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private airport transfer arranged to Siem Reap Boutique Stay with a welcome cold towel and refreshments in the vehicle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private check-in experience at the boutique hotel with a welcome drink and property orientation. After settling in, take a leisurely tuk-tuk ride through the charming streets of Siem Reap's Old French Quarter to get oriented. Visit the vibrant Psar Chaa (Old Market) area for a gentle introduction to local crafts, silks, and Cambodian artisan goods.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Pub Street and the surrounding lantern-lit alleyways. Enjoy a traditional Apsara dance performance over dinner at a premier cultural restaurant in town.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Welcome light lunch at the hotel's restaurant upon arrival — fresh tropical fruit platter, Cambodian spring rolls, and iced coconut water
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mahob Restaurant or Cuisine Wat Damnak — a refined tasting menu of modern Cambodian cuisine featuring amok, lok lak, and seasonal local ingredients, paired with Cambodian craft cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Ensure luggage is sent ahead to the room before sightseeing. Request hotel concierge to pre-book Apsara dinner show. November weather in Siem Reap is pleasantly cool and dry — ideal for exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Rise before dawn for a private sunrise visit to Angkor Wat — the world's largest religious monument. Arrive at Angkor Wat's reflecting pool by 05:30 with a private expert guide for the iconic sunrise spectacle. Explore the outer galleries, bas-reliefs depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk, and the central towers as the temple awakens in golden light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Angkor Thom — the great walled city — visiting the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces, the Baphuon, the Elephant Terrace, and the Terrace of the Leper King. Private guide provides deep historical and cultural context throughout. Midday retreat to a nearby luxury pavilion or return to hotel for a rest during peak heat hours.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the hotel rooftop or a curated lounge overlooking the Siem Reap River. Private dinner reservation at one of Siem Reap's finest establishments.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn breakfast box prepared by the hotel — croissants, fresh fruit, Cambodian iced coffee, and boiled eggs for the early temple visit
meals.lunch: Private picnic lunch arranged by the hotel near the Angkor complex, or dine at The Dining Room at Amansara (if accessible) — a refined set lunch with Cambodian and international options
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sugar Palm Restaurant — authentic Khmer cuisine in an elegant setting featuring kroeung-spiced dishes, fish with green mango salad, and sticky rice with mango for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a 3-day Angkor Archaeological Park pass. Wear light, breathable clothing and bring sunscreen, insect repellent, and a scarf for temple etiquette. Private guide and air-conditioned vehicle highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the jungle-clad temple of Ta Prohm — famously left intertwined with massive tree roots — for a mysterious and atmospheric experience. Continue to Preah Khan, a sprawling monastic complex with long corridors and detailed carvings, less visited and deeply atmospheric.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the exquisite Banteay Srei — the 'Citadel of Women' — located about 25 km north of Siem Reap. Renowned for its intricate pink sandstone carvings, considered the finest in all of Angkor. En route, stop at Banteay Samré temple. Return to hotel for an indulgent spa treatment — traditional Khmer massage or herbal compress therapy.
day_by_day.evening: Private cooking class experience at a premium Siem Reap culinary studio — learn to prepare three signature Cambodian dishes with a master chef, then enjoy the meal you've created.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the hotel — eggs to order, Cambodian rice porridge (bobor), fresh tropical juices, and pastries
meals.lunch: Lunch at a curated local restaurant near Banteay Srei — try Khmer red curry with jasmine rice and fresh coconut, or opt for a hotel-prepared gourmet picnic hamper
meals.dinner: The dishes prepared during the private cooking class, enjoyed in an intimate garden setting with Cambodian wine or imported selections

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei is a 45-minute drive from Siem Reap — plan accordingly. Book the spa and cooking class in advance through the hotel concierge. Bring cash for small artisan purchases near the temples.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise boat excursion on Tonlé Sap Lake — one of Southeast Asia's most remarkable inland seas. Glide through floating villages and observe the unique stilted communities, bird life, and fishermen at work. Visit the floating village of Kompong Khleang or Mechrey for an authentic and respectful cultural encounter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Siem Reap and visit the Angkor National Museum — a world-class institution housing thousands of Khmer artifacts, sculptures, and multimedia exhibits tracing the rise and fall of the Khmer Empire. Private guided tour for in-depth historical context.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the artisan quarter of Siem Reap — visit Artisans Angkor workshop and boutique to see skilled craftspeople preserving traditional Khmer arts including silk weaving, lacquerware, and stone carving. Purchase premium handcrafted souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel before the boat excursion — Cambodian rice porridge, fresh fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Haven Restaurant — a social enterprise training disadvantaged youth in hospitality, serving excellent Khmer and fusion cuisine in a warm, elegant setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Malis Restaurant — celebrated Cambodian chef Luu Meng's flagship restaurant showcasing elevated traditional Khmer recipes in a stunning open-air garden setting

day_by_day.notes: Bring binoculars for bird watching on Tonlé Sap. The lake is at its highest and most dramatic in November. Wear modest clothing for floating village visits. Artisans Angkor purchases directly support local artisan communities.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Koh Ker — a remote and rarely visited ancient capital 120 km northeast of Siem Reap. Explore the dramatic seven-tiered pyramid of Prasat Thom, rising 36 meters above the jungle canopy, and surrounding temple complexes largely reclaimed by forest. A truly off-the-beaten-path premium experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Beng Mealea — a vast 12th-century temple complex left almost entirely to nature, with trees growing through collapsed galleries and moss-covered stones. Far less visited than Angkor, creating an Indiana Jones-like atmosphere of discovery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap. Unwind with a sunset cocktail at the hotel. Quiet, restorative evening after a full day of exploration.

meals.breakfast: Packed gourmet breakfast from the hotel — prepared for the early departure to Koh Ker
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic hamper prepared by the hotel, enjoyed in a shaded area near the Koh Ker or Beng Mealea complex
meals.dinner: In-hotel dining — a private terrace dinner with a curated Cambodian and international menu, paired with premium wines

day_by_day.notes: The drive to Koh Ker is approximately 2.5 hours each way — depart by 07:00. Roads are sealed and comfortable. Hire the hotel's recommended private driver and guide. Bring plenty of water, sunscreen, and comfortable walking shoes. This is an adventurous full-day excursion.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Private transfer from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh by luxury road vehicle (approximately 5.5 hours) or take a scenic domestic flight (45 minutes) — recommended for premium comfort. En route or upon arrival, check into a luxury Phnom Penh hotel (e.g., Raffles Hotel Le Royal or Rosewood Phnom Penh).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — the stunning official residence of the King of Cambodia, featuring glittering spires, manicured gardens, and the famous Emerald Buddha. Explore the adjacent National Museum of Cambodia, housing the world's finest collection of Khmer sculpture and artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise on the Mekong and Tonlé Sap rivers aboard a private luxury boat. Watch the city's skyline glow as the rivers converge at Phnom Penh's iconic Chaktomuk confluence.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the Siem Reap hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch en route or upon arrival in Phnom Penh — dine at Topaz Restaurant, one of Phnom Penh's premier French-Cambodian fusion establishments
meals.dinner: Dinner aboard the private river cruise — curated Cambodian and international menu with Champagne and premium beverages

day_by_day.notes: Book the domestic flight in advance for convenience. The Royal Palace is closed on Monday and Friday mornings. Dress modestly for palace and pagoda visits — shoulders and knees must be covered. The sunset cruise should be booked through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Sobering but essential visit to the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) and the Choeung Ek Killing Fields — powerful and deeply moving memorials to the victims of the Khmer Rouge regime. A private expert guide provides historical context and ensures a respectful, meaningful visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the French colonial architecture of Phnom Penh's riverside promenade (Sisowath Quay). Visit the Central Market (Psar Thmei) — a stunning Art Deco building housing premium jewelry, silks, and local crafts. Browse premium boutiques along Street 240 for Cambodian designer goods and artisan pieces.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Phnom Penh's sophisticated dining and cocktail scene. Visit a rooftop bar for panoramic city views before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — eggs Benedict, tropical fruit, freshly baked pastries, and Cambodian iced coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Romdeng Restaurant — a social enterprise serving traditional Cambodian countryside cuisine in a beautifully restored colonial villa
meals.dinner: Dinner at Khéma La Poste — sophisticated French-Cambodian cuisine in a stunning heritage building, featuring premium seafood, foie gras, and an extensive wine list

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visits are emotionally intense — allow time for reflection. Audio guides are available and highly recommended. Photography is permitted in most areas but should be approached with sensitivity and respect.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Private transfer or domestic flight from Phnom Penh to Sihanoukville (approximately 4 hours by road or 1 hour by air), then onward by speedboat or private boat charter to Koh Rong Samloem or Song Saa Private Island — Cambodia's most exclusive beach destination. Check into a luxury overwater villa or eco-luxury beach resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the island resort and settle into your villa. Enjoy a welcome spa treatment — traditional Khmer herbal bath or ocean-view massage. Spend the afternoon on pristine white-sand beaches, swimming in crystal-clear turquoise waters.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset cocktails on the beach or villa deck. Watch the sun dip below the Gulf of Thailand horizon.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Phnom Penh hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Light lunch on arrival at the island resort — fresh seafood platter, tropical salads, and coconut-based drinks
meals.dinner: Private beach dinner under the stars — torchlit table on the sand with a bespoke seafood and Cambodian menu crafted by the resort's chef, paired with premium wines

day_by_day.notes: Song Saa Private Island is one of Southeast Asia's finest luxury island resorts — book well in advance. Koh Rong Samloem offers stunning bioluminescent plankton displays at night (seasonal). Pack light reef-safe sunscreen and snorkeling gear. November is an excellent month for Cambodian islands — dry season with calm seas.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided snorkeling or scuba diving excursion around the island's pristine coral reefs — teeming with tropical fish, sea turtles, and vibrant marine life. Alternatively, kayak through mangrove channels with a naturalist guide for an intimate nature experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend a leisurely afternoon at the resort — enjoy the infinity pool, indulge in a full spa journey (couples massage, facial, body scrub), or participate in a private guided meditation session on the beach. Optional: paddleboarding, sunset fishing, or a private catamaran charter around the island.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private cultural performance arranged by the resort — traditional Cambodian music and dance in an intimate beachfront setting. Enjoy a final island night under a canopy of stars.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast delivered to your villa deck — freshly baked croissants, tropical fruit, smoked salmon, eggs to order, and premium coffee
meals.lunch: Casual beachside lunch at the resort's open-air restaurant — grilled lobster, fresh ceviche, and tropical smoothies
meals.dinner: Overwater or beachfront gourmet dinner at the resort's signature restaurant — a chef's tasting menu featuring the day's freshest catch, Cambodian herbs, and imported delicacies paired with a curated wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Arrange scuba or snorkeling excursions through the resort's dive center. PADI certification available on-site if needed. Bring waterproof camera or GoPro. Check for bioluminescent plankton tours in the evening — a magical experience unique to this region.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on the island — enjoy a sunrise yoga session on the beach or a quiet walk along the shoreline. Last swim in the warm Gulf of Thailand waters. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Boat transfer back to Sihanoukville, then private vehicle or flight to Phnom Penh International Airport for onward international departure. Allow ample time for transfers — approximately 4-5 hours total travel time. Departure lounge access at the airport with premium amenities.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight — carry memories of Cambodia's ancient temples, vibrant culture, and pristine island paradise.

meals.breakfast: Final island breakfast at the resort — a leisurely spread of tropical fruits, pastries, eggs, and premium coffee enjoyed with ocean views
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort before departure, or a meal at Sihanoukville's best waterfront restaurant en route to the airport
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure flight details and allow extra time for island boat transfers and road travel. Purchase any remaining artisan goods, Cambodian pepper, or premium Kampot salt as gifts at the airport. Tip guides, drivers, and hotel staff generously — gratuities are an important part of the local service economy. Ensure all Angkor pass, museum tickets, and receipts are retained for memories.

query: Cambodia Angkor Wat + beaches, $1100, 10 days, November 2026
